stem.en: Two ships with engines are crossing at night in open water. The other ship is on your right. What should your ship do?

text.en: Hold course and speed, as the stand-on vessel

feedback.en: The stand-on vessel has the other ship on its left. Yours has it on the right.

text.en: Sound a signal and carry on as before

feedback.en: A signal does not decide who gives way, and your ship must still act.

text.en: Wait until the other ship turns first

feedback.en: Waiting is the danger here. The give-way vessel acts early.

text.en: Act early, as the give-way vessel

feedback.en: Yes. With the other ship on your right, you are the give-way vessel.

explanation.en: In a crossing, the ship with the other on its right is the give-way vessel and acts early to keep clear. The other ship is the stand-on vessel and holds its course and speed.

hints.en: Which side is the other ship on?
Other ship on your right: you give way.
